brief_title: Fighting Osteoporosis With Risedronate Co-Therapy During Incretin
official_title: Bisphosphonate Co-Therapy to Preserve Musculoskeletal Health in Older Adults Using Tirzepatide

primary_outcomes.measure: Change in Hip Bone Mineral Density

brief_summary: Tirzepatide produces rapid, clinically meaningful weight loss. In older adults, however, substantial weight reduction may accelerate loss of bone and muscle, increase frailty risk, and compound age-related skeletal vulnerability. The purpose of this study is to find out if taking risedronate along with tirzepatide preserves musculoskeletal health during tirzepatide-associated weight loss.

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* BMI≥30 or 27.0-29.9 kg/m2 plus one weight related co-morbidity
* Weight stability (within 5% in past 3 months)
* Community dwelling
* English speaking
* Able to attend regular in person appointments, willingness to take tirzepatide and risedronate medication, and willing to provide informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Weight \>450 lbs (DXA limit)
* Disordered alcohol or substance use
* Eating disorder in past 5 years
* \>1 fall (injurious or non-injurious) in past year or prior fragility fracture
* Osteoporosis (self-report, medication use, or T-score ≤ -2.5 on hip or spine DXA scan)
* Use of oral corticosteroids (\>5 d/month in past 3 months), use of incretin analog (GLP1Ra or dual agonist) in past 24 months, use of any AOM or prescription osteoporosis medication in last 12 months, history of intolerance or adverse reaction to GLP1Ra (other incretin analog) or bisphosphonate, concomitant use of insulin secretagogues or insulin
